feature: The card mark — Game Changer, mass land denial, extra turns
note:
The surfaces that draw `CardFactMark`, which must draw the SAME one: the decklist row, /collection's row and tile, and the card modal — plus the two `MarkKey` mounts that gloss it, which are the reason a wordless mark is legal here at all.

PRECONDITION, and it is the one that decides whether this sheet proves anything: the account must OWN a card carrying a fact. Measured 2026-09-20 on both `staging` and `local-dev` — the reference account owns 8 Game Changers, 1 mass land denial and 8 extra turns out of ~2,805 cards, so a mark IS reachable on both. But 17 marked cards in 2,805 means a sheet taken on an arbitrary page of /collection photographs NO mark and reads as coverage while proving nothing. Every /collection row here searches for a known marked card first rather than trusting the default page — the same trap `proxy-mark.json` records for `deck_proxies`, arriving by rarity instead of by an empty table.

CARD_MARK_DECK must be a deck that HOLDS a marked card. A deck of 99 cards holding none is the common case, not the exception, so this cannot be any deck.

The key rows are separate from the mark rows deliberately. `check:shared` reads each row's own `view`, and the key is mounted by two different files — `decklist.tsx` builds its entries and `collection-mark-key.tsx` builds /collection's. A single row naming one of them would leave the other free to stop glossing while the gate stayed green, which is precisely the failure the deck-status marks shipped with.

shares.note: Every surface renders it as-is — the tooltip wraps it on the decklist row but does not replace it — so the check is asked of the file each row already names.

rows.label: /decks/[id] — the mark on a decklist row, after the count
/decks/[id] — the key that glosses all three, with or without a marked row
/collection?view=rows — the mark after the name, before the availability marker
/collection — the same mark on a tile's meta line, at the 12px floor
